views.thesis: ETF, judged as crude exposure, not a company. Fact: Brent was ~$110.74 on Oct 21 and ~$92.4-92.5 on Nov 16-17 (WTI $85.72), after a 16% weekly drop in early November as Hormuz flows and OPEC output recovered; IEA sees a 1.7 mb/d surplus in Q4 2026 and Goldman forecasts $88 Brent for 2027. Inference: the 12-1 momentum that ranks USO #1 is the 2026 Iran-war premium, which is now unwinding; the factor score is backward-looking.
views.risks: Two-sided headline risk: reported (unverified) mine strikes in Hormuz or a breakdown in US-Iran restraint would spike crude. No settlement price found after Nov 17. Roll yield/backwardation effect not checked.

views.thesis: Fact: Q3 2026 (reported Oct 30) adjusted EPS $5.28, operating cash flow ~$16bn, net debt cut $7.8bn, buybacks ~$2.5bn; downstream earned ~$4.9bn on high refining margins. Inference: the +35% revenue / +180% net income growth and 8% FCF yield the engine rewards are peak-cycle numbers earned at ~$100+ Brent; with Brent now ~$92 and a forecast surplus, forward earnings are likely lower, so the stock is fairly priced rather than cheap. Balance sheet and payout are solid, which argues against an outright avoid.
views.risks: Falling crude and refining margins; shares fell ~4% on Nov 18 with oil. Upside risk if Hormuz disruption returns. Forward consensus EPS not found.

views.thesis: Fact: Q3 2026 revenue +39% to $24.4bn; FY2026 revenue guidance raised to $91-92bn from $85-87bn; oral GLP-1 Foundayo already at $184m quarterly sales; retatrutide Phase 3 positive. Forward P/E cited ~33x versus a 5-year average of ~40x. Inference: the only large-cap in scope with accelerating organic growth that is unrelated to oil or AI capex; quality is real, not an artefact.
views.risks: Valuation: average analyst target cited ~$1,330-1,337 is below the $1,349.98 snapshot price, so upside depends on further estimate raises. Headline non-GAAP EPS guide was trimmed to $35.00-36.00 by ~$4.2bn acquired IPR&D charges. Zepbound realised prices falling; drug-pricing policy. Stock closed at a high of $1,443.50 on Nov 13 and is ~6% lower in the snapshot.

views.thesis: Fact: Q3 2026 EPS $0.49 vs an expected loss, MLR 84.0% (88.5% a year ago), FY2026 earnings-from-operations guidance raised a third time to $850-950m; 2027 rates up ~14% on average. But $250m of Q3 revenue was a risk-adjustment estimate change and guidance implies a sizeable Q4 loss. Inference: the 53% 'FCF yield' and net-cash figures that drive its value z-score of 2.25 are insurer float (premiums and risk-adjustment payables), not distributable cash - the factor score overstates cheapness. On operating earnings it is still inexpensive, hence neutral rather than avoid.
views.risks: Policy: CMS 'CRUSH' anti-fraud proposed rule (Nov 16) covers the ACA marketplace as well as Medicare Advantage; ACA subsidy outcome unresolved. Risk-adjustment true-ups can reverse. Stock -25% in a month with 63% vol; reported CFO share sale (date unverified). Reason for the full November drop not conclusively verified.

views.thesis: Fact: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS $4.23 vs ~$3.90 expected, FCF $19.1bn, $9.4bn returned in the quarter, $20bn buyback planned for 2027, Q4 dividend raised to $1.07; net debt $22.1bn. Energy Products earnings jumped to $9.1bn from $4.1bn while upstream fell to $7.3bn. Inference: the beat was a refining-margin windfall from the supply disruption; with crude down ~15% in November and margins likely to normalise, trailing growth and yield overstate forward earnings. Committed buyback and balance sheet limit downside.
views.risks: Crude and crack spreads falling; shares fell ~4% on Nov 18. Upside if Middle East supply is disrupted again. Forward consensus not found.

views.thesis: Fact: Q3 2026 operating profit fell 6% to $12.71bn (underwriting profit -43%, Geico pretax -45%) but beat the FactSet estimate; Berkshire repurchased $9.6bn of stock in Q3 plus ~$2bn in October, and held $356.9bn of cash at end-September. Inference: record buybacks signal management sees the shares below intrinsic value, and the cash pile both earns a high short rate and is optionality in a market where breadth above MA50 is 12%. Lowest-vol name in scope (15%).
views.risks: Insurance margins deteriorating (Geico loss costs and ad spend); the +79% net income growth in the engine is investment mark-to-market, not operations. Data flag: market_cap in the candidates file ($0.8bn) is wrong, so any value metric for this row is unusable.

views.thesis: Fact: Q3 2026 revenue $4.87bn (+19%) vs $4.75bn expected, gross booking value +21% to $27.7bn, nights booked +16% (about +13% excluding Reserve Now Pay Later); FY revenue growth outlook raised to high-teens, adjusted EBITDA margin ~36%, new $12bn buyback authorisation (about 12% of the $100.6bn market cap in the file). Net cash $4.9bn. Inference: growth is re-accelerating with a capital-return backstop at a ~5% FCF yield.
views.risks: Management said Q3 was the peak of the pay-later net benefit, so Q4 nights growth guides lower (at least low-double-digit) as cancellations catch up; EPS was flattered by a $135m lower tax provision. Discretionary travel is exposed if the selloff and ~5% 10-year yields hit consumers. Figures from secondary coverage of the shareholder letter.

views.thesis: Fact: Q3 2026 sales $25.4bn (+5.9%), adjusted EPS $2.59 (down ~7.5% y/y), GAAP EPS $0.09 after $5.5bn litigation charges; FY2026 guidance raised to sales $101.0-101.4bn and adjusted EPS $11.05-11.15. Inference: the engine's -96% net income growth (growth z -1.25) is a one-off talc charge and understates the business, but at $270.77 the stock is ~24x the guidance midpoint (my arithmetic) for mid-single-digit growth - a fair defensive, not a bargain.
views.risks: Talc resolution ($5.5bn+ for ~76,000 claims) is still a proposal; Stelara biosimilars; Orthopaedics separation. Dec 8, 2026 investor event will give 2027 guidance - a known catalyst date.

views.thesis: Fact: revenue is shrinking (-19% y/y in the file); the 'record' June-quarter profit of $389.6m included a $268.4m unrealised derivative gain on eBay stock (adjusted $179.3m). GameStop's $56bn bid for eBay was rejected and it has since built a stake reported at ~$4.9-5bn (7-10% depending on source) alongside ~$5bn cash and ~$3bn debt as of Aug 1. Inference: trend, relative strength and the 7.5% earnings yield are driven by the eBay campaign and mark-to-market gains, not the operating business - a takeover-saga/quality trap, and the equity is now a concentrated, partly debt-funded bet on one stock in a falling market.
views.risks: Upside risk from retail squeezes and CEO Ryan Cohen's open-market buying (>5m shares in 2026). A proxy fight or new bid for eBay is an open-ended event. Could not find any October-November 2026 news on the eBay situation.

views.thesis: Fact: October retail-month net sales $24.50bn (+12.6%); first nine weeks of fiscal Q1 +12.8%; comps +7.3% excluding gasoline and FX (gas inflation added ~3.9 points to the reported 11.1%); digital +22.5%. Inference: operating momentum is excellent, but the file shows a 1.9% earnings yield (~53x trailing) with the 10-year Treasury near 5%, and the stock is 0.75% off its high and 12% above MA50 - it is being bought as a shelter, leaving little margin for error.
views.risks: Multiple compression if yields rise further or the defensive bid unwinds; headline comps are inflated by fuel prices. Fiscal Q1 report inferred for Dec 10 (not company-confirmed).

views.thesis: Fact: fiscal Q4 2026 results are due Wednesday Nov 25, when the first fiscal 2027 outlook is expected. At Q3 Deere raised FY2026 net income guidance to $4.75-5.00bn, said 2026 marks the bottom of the large-ag cycle, and flagged tariff expense rising from ~$750m net in FY2026 to a ~$1bn run rate in FY2027; FY2026 included $382m of tariff refunds. Inference: a cyclical-trough story priced at ~33x trailing earnings (3.0% earnings yield in the file) needs a strong FY2027 guide; no edge on that guide, so neutral until it is known.
views.risks: EARNINGS IN 3 TRADING DAYS (2026-11-25) - stage around it. Tariff costs, farm income, higher financing rates for equipment buyers; net debt $55bn is mostly the captive finance arm.

views.thesis: Fact: fiscal Q3 2027 reported Nov 19: revenue $188.8bn (+5.2%), adjusted operating income +5.5%, US e-commerce +23%, marketplace/fulfilment services +49%; FY guidance raised to net sales +4.9-5.2% and adjusted EPS $2.84-2.89. Inference: fresh beat-and-raise removes near-term earnings risk and the business gains share when consumers trade down; one of few names with positive 1-month return (+6%). Conviction capped by valuation: ~45x the guidance midpoint at $128.38 (my arithmetic).
views.risks: Rich multiple with the 10-year near 5%; reported operating income +16% is flattered by a $700m PhonePe charge a year ago; management cited >$2bn of extra diesel/transport cost this year. Post-earnings share reaction not found.

views.thesis: ETF, judged as US utilities exposure. Fact: the Fed held at 3.75-4.00% on Oct 28 with two dissents in favour of a hike, and the 10-year yield was reported at 5.03% after the decision; on Nov 10 utilities fell as yields rebounded and on worries about a slowdown in AI infrastructure build-out. Inference: low volatility (16%) makes it a relative shelter, but the sector is squeezed from both sides - bond-proxy valuation against a ~5% risk-free rate, and the data-centre load-growth premium is exposed to the same AI unwind driving the selloff. Flat price over 1, 3 and 12 months is consistent with that.
views.risks: Further rate hikes (hawkish dissenters); AI power-demand de-rating of the largest holdings; conversely a growth scare that pulls yields down would help. Current 10-year yield and XLU dividend yield not verified for Nov 20.

views.thesis: Fact: Q3 2026 revenue +6.7% to $22.9bn, adjusted EPS $1.69 vs $1.63 expected; FY2026 guidance raised to revenue ~$92.6bn, adjusted EPS ~$7.28 and adjusted FCF ~$6.1bn; Q4 guide above consensus. Inference: at $106.46 that is ~14.6x guided EPS (my arithmetic) with a ~7% FCF yield, estimates moving up and the deliberate Amazon volume reduction largely behind it - cheap, improving and not AI- or oil-beta.
views.risks: US average daily volume still expected down y/y in Q4; GAAP EPS $1.37 after a $182m goodwill impairment and transformation costs; high diesel prices; peak-season execution; freight is cyclical if the selloff reaches the real economy. Dividend coverage not checked.

views.thesis: Fact: on Nov 16 CMS released the 'CRUSH' proposed rule (CMS-6098-P), projecting ~$90bn of savings over 10 years and expanding authority to audit Medicare Advantage insurers and recover overpayments, reportedly back to payment year 2018; UNH fell 5-10% on individual days that week and is -20% over the month. CMS premiums were 44% of 2025 revenue and the company has not sized the impact. Revenue is flat y/y in the file. Inference: the 'value' the engine sees (7.5% FCF yield) sits on earnings that now carry an unquantified retroactive liability; cheap for a reason until the rule is sized.
views.risks: Rule is only proposed (comments due Jan 19, 2027) and earlier RADV rules were judged manageable, so a relief rally is possible. Also the weak 2027 MA rate notice from January. No analyst estimate of the clawback found.

views.thesis: Fact: Q3 2026 non-GAAP EPS $1.45 (+8%); FY guidance raised to ~$5.60 from $5.38 - about 9.6x at $53.61 (my arithmetic), 14% FCF yield in the file. But online branded checkout volume grew only 1-2% for a fourth straight quarter, revenue growth is 2%, and new CEO Enrique Lores plans to accelerate investment in 2027. Inference: optically the cheapest stock in scope, but the core franchise is not growing and 2027 margins are guided to absorb more spend - a classic value-trap profile until branded checkout turns.
views.risks: A July 2026 headline referred to a Stripe takeover bid for PayPal; I could not verify its current status - if live, the share price embeds deal optionality and would fall if it lapses. EU de minimis change (~70bp headwind), competition from Apple Pay/Shop Pay.

views.thesis: Fact: Q3 2026 net income $15.3bn (+6%), diluted EPS $5.57 (Zacks: adjusted $5.75, below its $5.94 consensus); NII +13% to $27.1bn and FY2026 NII guidance raised to ~$106.2bn, with ~$107bn ex-Markets pencilled for 2027; expenses +12%, a $539m reserve build mainly in Wholesale, fixed-income trading -4%. Inference: higher-for-longer rates support NII, but expense growth is outrunning revenue and wholesale credit is being reserved for as equity markets fall - balanced. The negative FCF yield in the file is a bank balance-sheet artefact and should be ignored.
views.risks: Credit cycle if the selloff spreads (bank CEOs warned on rates and inflation; private-credit outflows reported); capital-markets revenue in a VIX-36 tape. 2027 NII figure is from one secondary source.

views.thesis: Block. Fact: Q3 2026 (reported Nov 3) gross profit +22% to ~$3.24bn, Cash App gross profit +27%, record 29% adjusted operating margin; FY2026 guidance raised a third time to gross profit $12.626bn and adjusted EPS $4.15 (~17x at $70.46, my arithmetic). But Q4 gross profit growth is guided to ~15% and the preliminary 2027 outlook is 'at least 15%', while transaction, loan and receivable losses rose 66%. Inference: reasonable price for a decelerating grower whose incremental growth comes from consumer lending - not attractive to add into a risk-off tape.
views.risks: Consumer credit losses on Cash App Borrow/Afterpay if the economy weakens; bitcoin gross profit halved to $52m and the stock trades with crypto (sector -35% in a month). GAAP earnings yield only 1.1%.
